relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.evidence: Rahul Sankrityayan who acted as a mentor to Jagdish and advised him to travel to Sri Lanka which he did in 1933.

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.evidence: In Sri Lanka, Jagdish became an ordained monk and was given the title of tipitik acharya. He was ordained by Venerable L. Dhammananda Nayaka Mahathero.

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.evidence: During his time at the Vidyalankara Pirivena he translated the Digha Nikāya into Hindi.

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.role: Professor of Pali and Buddhist Philosophy
relations.evidence: While in Sarnath he also worked for Benares Hindu University to offer courses in Pāli... the University had been forced to appoint a Professor of Pali and Buddhist Philosophy

relations.subject: Sangharakshita
relations.evidence: During this time Kashyap took on a young English monk as a live-in student for about nine months. Sangharakshita went on to found the Western Buddhist Order in 1968, and considers Kashyap to have been an important teacher

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.evidence: Kashyap offered to teach Pāli at Gaya College and at Nalanda College in Bihar-Sharif.

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.evidence: He played a major role in the establishment of the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara... when the Bihar state government decided to start an institute for Pāli studies at Nalanda, he was the obvious choice to head the project. In 1951 the institute became the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.evidence: in 1959 was asked to become the first Professor of Pāli and Buddhism at the Sanskrit University of Varanasi. He remained there until 1965

relations.subject: Jagdish Kashyap
relations.evidence: when he returned to Nalanda for a second term as Director of the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He retired in 1973.
